arxiv-1412-7208.title: Averaging in LRS class II spacetimes
arxiv-1412-7208.creator: Petr Kašpar †, Otakar Svítek §
arxiv-1412-7208.description: Abstract We generalize Buchert’s averaged equations [Gen. Rel. Grav. 32, 105 (2000); Gen. Rel. Grav. 33, 1381 (2001)] to LRS class II dust model in the sense that all Einstein equations are averaged, not only the trace part. We derive the relevant averaged equations and we investigate backreaction on expansion and shear scalars in an approximate LTB model.

arxiv-1808-03324.title: Topological Graphic Passwords And Their Matchings Towards Cryptography Manuscript received June 1, 2017; revised August 26, 2017. Corresponding author: Bing Yao, email: yybb918@163.com.
arxiv-1808-03324.creator: Bing Yao 1,5 , Hui Sun 1 , Xiaohui Zhang 1 , Yarong Mu 1 , Yirong Sun 1 Hongyu Wang 2,‡ , Jing Su 2 , Mingjun Zhang 3 , Sihua Yang 3 , Chao Yang 4
arxiv-1808-03324.description: Abstract Graphical passwords (GPWs) are convenient for mobile equipments with touch screen. Topological graphic passwords (Topsnut-gpws) can be saved in computer by classical matrices and run quickly than the existing GPWs. We research Topsnut-gpws by the matching of view, since they have many advantages. We discuss: configuration matching partition, coloring/labelling matching partition, set matching partition, matching chain, etc.

arxiv-2103-04223.title: Phonon Hall Viscosity in Magnetic Insulators
arxiv-2103-04223.creator: Mengxing Ye, Lucile Savary, Leon Balents
arxiv-2103-04223.description: Abstract The Phonon Hall Viscosity is the leading term evincing time-reversal symmetry breaking in the low energy description of lattice phonons. It may generate phonon Berry curvature, and can be observed experimentally through the acoustic Faraday effect and thermal Hall transport.

arxiv-2110-08814.title: TEAM-Net: Multi-modal Learning for Video Action Recognition with Partial Decoding
arxiv-2110-08814.creator: Zhengwei Wang, Qi She, Aljosa Smolic
arxiv-2110-08814.description: Abstract Most of existing video action recognition models ingest raw RGB frames. However, the raw video stream requires enormous storage and contains significant temporal redundancy. Video compression (e.g., H.264, MPEG-4) reduces superfluous information by representing the raw video stream using the concept of Group of Pictures (GOP).

arxiv-2112-10808.title: Radial Distribution of the Dust Comae of Comets 45P/Honda-Mrkos-Pajdus̆áková and 46P/Wirtanen Journal: PSJ
arxiv-2112-10808.creator: C. Lejoly, W. Harris, N. Samarasinha, B.E.A. Mueller, E. Howell, J. Bodnarik, A. Springmann, T. Kareta, B. Sharkey, J. Noonan, L. R. Bedin, J.-G. Bosch, A. Brosio, E. Bryssinck, J.-B. de Vanssay, F.-J. Hambsch, O. Ivanova, V. Krushinsky, Z.-Y. Lin, F. Manzini, A. Maury, N. Moriya, P. Ochner, V. Olda
arxiv-2112-10808.description: Abstract There was an unprecedented opportunity to study the inner dust coma environment, where the dust and gas are not entirely decoupled, of comets 45P/Honda-Mrkos-Pajdus̆áková (45P/HMP) from Dec. 26, 2016 - Mar. 15, 2017, and 46P/Wirtanen from Nov. 10, 2018 - Feb. 13, 2019, both in visible wavelengths.

arxiv-2208-05776.title: Neural Networks for Scalar Input and Functional Output
arxiv-2208-05776.creator: Sidi Wu, Cédric Beaulac, Jiguo Cao
arxiv-2208-05776.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sidi Wu, Cédric Beaulac, Jiguo Cao. The regression of a functional response on a set of scalar predictors can be a challenging task, especially if there is a large number of predictors, or the relationship between those predictors and the response is nonlinear. In this work, we propose a solution to this problem: a feed-forward neural network (NN) designed to predict a functional response using scalar inputs.

arxiv-2306-07878.title: Deep Learning-Enabled Zero-Touch Device Identification: Mitigating the Impact of Channel Variability Through MIMO Diversity
arxiv-2306-07878.creator: Bechir Hamdaoui, Nora Basha, Kathiravetpillai Sivanesan
arxiv-2306-07878.description: Abstract Deep learning-enabled device fingerprinting has proven efficient in enabling automated identification and authentication of transmitting devices. It does so by leveraging the transmitters’ unique features that are inherent to hardware impairments caused during manufacturing to extract device-specific signatures that can be exploited to uniquely distinguish and separate between (identical) devices.

arxiv-2408-12998.title: Tight Bounds for Constant-Round Domination on Graphs of High Girth and Low Expansion
arxiv-2408-12998.creator: Christoph Lenzen and Sophie Wenning
arxiv-2408-12998.description: Abstract A long-standing open question is which graph class is the most general one permitting constant-time constant-factor approximations for dominating sets. The approximation ratio has been bounded by increasingly general parameters such as genus, arboricity, or expansion of the input graph.

arxiv-2412-20789.title: Pre-trained Audio Transformer as a Foundational AI Tool for Gravitational Waves
arxiv-2412-20789.creator: Chayan Chatterjee, Abigail Petulante, Yang Hu, Roy Lau, Suyash Deshmukh, Haowei Fu, Trang Hoang, Stephen Chong Zhao, Jesse Spencer-Smith, Karan Jani
arxiv-2412-20789.description: Abstract As gravitational wave detectors become more advanced and sensitive, the number of signals recorded by Advanced LIGO and Virgo from merging compact objects is expected to rise dramatically. This surge in detection rates necessitates the development of adaptable, scalable, and efficient tools capable of addressing a wide range of tasks in gravitational wave astronomy.

arxiv-2501-01147.title: Integrated AHB to APB Bridge Using Raspberry Pi and Artix-7 FPGA
arxiv-2501-01147.creator: Gopi Chand Ananthu, Riadul Islam
arxiv-2501-01147.description: Abstract This project focuses on the design and implementation of an AHB to APB Bridge for efficient communication in System-on-Chip (SoC) architectures. The Advanced High-performance Bus (AHB) is used for high-speed operations, typically connecting processors and memory, while the Advanced Peripheral Bus (APB) is optimized for low-power, low-speed peripheral devices.

arxiv-2509-17023.title: Magnetic Frustration in CuYbSe 2 : an Yb-Based Triangular Lattice Selenide
arxiv-2509-17023.creator: Barkha Khattar, Anzar Ali, Masahiko Isobe, Yogesh Singh
arxiv-2509-17023.description: Abstract The Yb based triangular lattice delafossites A A Yb X 2 X_{2} ( A A = alkali metal, X X = O, S, Se) have recently been studied as quantum spin liquid candidates. We report the synthesis of powders and single crystals of CuYbSe 2 with a perfect triangular lattice of Yb 3+ moments.

arxiv-2510-09808.title: IECZ–III: Hardcore Condensation Lift Distributional and parameterized hardness with size-aware invariants
arxiv-2510-09808.creator: Marko Lela (ORCID: 0009-0008-0768-5184 )
arxiv-2510-09808.description: Abstract This paper develops a compact, size-aware blueprint for transferring structure through gadget lifts. Two low-order invariants—cumulative mod- q q Fourier mass up to degree k k and noise stability Stab ρ \mathrm{Stab}_{\rho} —are treated as a reusable “profile”, tied to the gadget’s affine interface.

arxiv-2510-20913.title: Multiwavelength view of circumstellar interaction in supernovae
arxiv-2510-20913.creator: Poonam Chandra 0000-0002-0844-6563
arxiv-2510-20913.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Poonam Chandra 0000-0002-0844-6563. The interaction of post-explosion supernova ejecta with the surrounding circumstellar medium creates emission across the electromagnetic spectrum. Since the circumstellar medium is created by the mass lost from the progenitor star, it carries tell-tale signatures of the progenitor. Consequently, observations and modeling of radiation produced by the interaction in various types of supernovae have provided valuable insights into their progenitors.

arxiv-2511-01816.title: No-Rank Tensor Decomposition Using Metric Learning
arxiv-2511-01816.creator: Maryam Bagherian
arxiv-2511-01816.description: Abstract . Tensor decomposition faces fundamental challenges in analyzing high-dimensional data, where traditional methods based on reconstruction and fixed-rank constraints often fail to capture semantically meaningful structures. This paper introduces a no-rank tensor decomposition framework grounded in metric learning, which replaces reconstruction objectives with a discriminative, similarity-based optimization.

arxiv-2602-20933.title: Dropping Anchor and Spherical Harmonics for Sparse-view Gaussian Splatting
arxiv-2602-20933.creator: Shuangkang Fang, I-Chao Shen, Xuanyang Zhang, Zesheng Wang, Yufeng Wang, Wenrui Ding, Gang Yu, Takeo Igarashi
arxiv-2602-20933.description: Abstract Recent 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) Dropout methods address overfitting under sparse-view conditions by randomly nullifying Gaussian opacities. However, we identify a neighbor compensation effect in these approaches: dropped Gaussians are often compensated by their neighbors, weakening the intended regularization. Moreover, these methods overlook the contribution of high-degree spherical harmonic coefficients (SH) to overfitting.

pmc-11475606.creator: Shuai Yang, Yi Yang, Bin Feng, Lu Hu, Xin Dong, Huiqin Dong, Wenke Bai
pmc-11475606.description: Simple SummaryShiqu County, in Sichuan Province, is the eastern edge of the distribution area of the kiang (Equus kiang) on the Tibetan Plateau. pmc-11486367.creator: David Suh, Dong-Won Kim, Seung-Mi Lee, Yu-Seon Jung, Sun-Young Jung, Chul-Min Kim
pmc-11486367.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). pmc-11489692.title: A chromosome-scale genome assembly of the peanut beetle, Ulomoides dermestoides (Coleptera: Tenebrionidae)
pmc-11489692.creator: Huamei Xiao, Chunhui Ma, Shuangyuan Li, Huangjie Gao, Shaomin Tao, Chuanlin Yin
pmc-11489692.description: Ulomoides dermestoides, a member of the Tenebrionidae family, is known by various common names such as Chinese beetle, Chinese weevil, peanut beetle, cancer beetle, or asthma beetle. Despite its origin in Asia, it has achieved global distribution owing to its perceived medicinal properties.

pmc-11506834.title: Antagonistic Feedback Control of Muscle Length Changes for Efficient Involuntary Posture Stabilization
pmc-11506834.creator: Masami Iwamoto, Noritoshi Atsumi, Daichi Kato, Yong Peng, Danqi Wang, Dongkai Chu, Honghao Zhang
pmc-11506834.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simultaneous and cooperative muscle activation results in involuntary posture stabilization in vertebrates. However, the mechanism through which more muscles than joints contribute to this stabilization remains unclear. We developed a computational human body model with 949 muscle action lines and 22 joints and examined muscle activation patterns for stabilizing right upper or lower extremity motions at a neutral body posture (NBP) under gravity using actor–critic reinforcement learning (ACRL).

pmc-11680253.title: Mechanism and Kinetics of HIV-1 Protease Activation
pmc-11680253.creator: Caroline O. Tabler, John C. Tilton
pmc-11680253.description: The HIV-1 protease is a critical enzyme for viral replication. Because protease activity is necessary to generate mature infectious virions, it is a primary target of antiretroviral treatment. Here, we provide an overview of the mechanisms regulating protease activation and the methods available to assess protease activity.

pmc-11714835.title: Predicting Mild Cognitive Impairment in Amyloid Beta Biomarker Positive Individuals Using Automated Speech‐Based Testing Procedures
pmc-11714835.creator: Caroline Skirrow, Udeepa Meepegama, Michael T Ropacki, Jack Weston, Emil Fristed
pmc-11714835.description: BackgroundNew disease modifying treatments for Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) require confirmation of amyloid biomarkers and evidence of clinical and/or cognitive AD symptoms. Blood tests for AD biomarkers are poised to enter routine care. However, at‐risk individuals with positive biomarkers vary in their level of cognitive impairment, raising the need for sensitive and scalable cognitive assessments.

pmc-13049647.title: Metabolic engineering of Methanothermobacter thermautotrophicus ΔH for recombinant acetoin production
pmc-13049647.creator: Tina Baur, Maximilliene T Allaart, Aaron Zipperle, Gabriela Contreras, Christian Fink, Largus T Angenent, Bastian Molitor
pmc-13049647.description: Thermophilic methanogens of the genus Methanothermobacter are established biocatalysts in power-to-gas applications, converting H2 and CO2 into CH4 through the process of methanogenesis. Further expanding this platform for the bioproduction of value-added compounds (power-to-x) has the potential to increase the economic viability of such processes. This requires a genetic toolset that enables the controlled expression of recombinant pathways.
